text.p: Brisbane broker Wilson HTM Ltd said it was recommending shares of Savage Resources Ltd as a buy investment, reflecting significant long-term growth potential for the diversified miner and zinc refiner.

"Savage has an exceptional asset base on which to build long-term growth. High profile assets have significant long-term growth potential," Wilson's resources research director, Phil Hutchings, said in a research report.
Earnings growth would continue to be driven from higher low lost production at all Savage's operations, Hutchings said.

Savage's SVR Zinc Inc operations which consisted of three mines and a modern electrolytic refinery in the United States, was already profitable and were well positioned to capitalise on the strength of the zinc price, Hutchings said.

Coal operations in Australia's Hunter Valley produced semi-soft and thermal coal for Asian export markets with production set to double late in 1997 following the first commercial production from the Glendell mine, adjacent to Savage's Liddell pit.

The company's 49 percent of the Ernest Henry copper/gold mine, which was expected to be commissioned in December, would contribute about 47,500 tonnes of copper concentrate and 60,000 ounces of gold, the report said.

"Longer term prospects are excellent with aggressive exploration programmes centred on Australia and the Americas," he said. "Even without a surge in the zinc price, Savage remains a fundamentally attractive investment," Hutchings said.
Savage reported a net profit of A$5.52 million in the yalf year to December 31, down from A$11.15 million a year earlier.
Net profit in the year to June 1996 was A$23.1 million, up from A$8.18 million a year earlier.
At the time of Wilson's report, Savage's share price was A$1.25. The stock opened at A$1.31 on Tuesday, down a cent.
